title: Hello lock: the smallest lock
what: A door lock on a chip: it opens when someone types the secret code A5. In the protected version, three separate checks must all agree.
why: If one wire decides 'open', one glitch on that wire opens the door without the code.
teaches: Redundancy only helps when the copies are really separate: one glitch beats one check, but not three.

runs.label: 2. Run the protected lock
runs.expect: 3 glitches needed (plain build); the optimised build merges the copies and needs only 1

lesson_after: Compare the two runs. The weak lock opens with a single glitch on its one 'open' flip-flop. The protected lock needs three glitches, one per copy, as long as the copies stay separate. Look at 'Did the protection survive the build?': the optimising build (synth) merges the three copies into one, and the lock is weak again. The fix is named under 'What to do': keep the copies in separate modules and stop the tool from merging them, then check the final netlist again.
